findings.issue: The end-to-end chain relies on the gateway appending its socket peer to X-Forwarded-For. Spring Cloud Gateway 5.0.2 webflux (in the Gradle cache) most likely does not: its jar contains TrustedProxies$XForwardedTrustedProxiesCondition$OnTrustedProxiesNotEmpty, TrustedProxies$NotXForwardedTrustedProxiesCondition and RemoveXForwardedHeadersFilter (CVE-2025-41235 hardening): XForwardedHeadersFilter is registered only when spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.trusted-proxies is set; otherwise X-Forwarded-* is stripped from the proxied request. Nothing in the repo sets trusted-proxies. Likely result on AWS and Compose: user-service receives no X-Forwarded-For, ClientIp falls back to the gateway pod/container IP, genuine claims are refused with REFERRAL_IP_MATCH when view and claim pass the same gateway instance, and farming is no longer limited by IP. No test exercises the gateway hop.
findings.fix: Confirm in the 5.0.2 sources first. Then either (a) configure trusted-proxies for the VPC/ALB range (Helm) and the Compose network, checking the effect on Reactor Netty's remote address and RateLimitWebFilter; or (b) have the gateway compute the client with RateLimitWebFilter's right-hand rule and forward it in a header under the already-stripped x-internal- prefix (e.g. X-Internal-Client-Ip), read only by user-service. Add a gateway integration test with a stub downstream, and one assertion through the gateway that the real client (not spoofed, not the gateway IP) is hashed.

findings.issue: Pre-existing, out of scope, same root cause: the Google OIDC callback depends on auth-service receiving X-Forwarded-Host/Proto/Port through the gateway; if RemoveXForwardedHeadersFilter is active these are stripped too and the callback is built from the downstream Host (auth-service:8081, http).
findings.fix: File in the tech-debt register; make the fix for the major cover the OIDC callback; post-deploy check of the callback URL.

summary: Request changes. The round-2 major is fixed per service (user-service and gateway strategy none; ReferralForwardedForTomcatTest really exercises RemoteIpValve). Gateway-side 'none' is safe for RateLimitWebFilter, CORS and redirects. Not confirmed, with a likely break: Spring Cloud Gateway 5.0.2 adds X-Forwarded headers only when trusted-proxies is configured and otherwise strips them, so user-service probably sees only the gateway IP. Configure trusted-proxies or forward a gateway-computed x-internal- header, and test through the gateway. Evidence: class names in spring-cloud-gateway-server-webflux-5.0.2.jar (jar listing; not decompiled).
